quiz.title: Rate of Change Quiz (Exercise 6.1)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on rate of change of quantities: dA/dt, dV/dt, perimeter and related rates. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Application of Derivatives, Exercise 6.1 (rate of change)

questions.q: The radius of a circle grows at 3 cm/s. How fast is the area changing when the radius is 10 cm?
The side of a square increases at 4 cm/s. How fast is the perimeter increasing?
questions.explanation: P = 4x, so dP/dt = 4(dx/dt) = 4(4) = 16 cm/s. The perimeter rate is constant here, independent of the side length.

questions.q: The edge of a cube is expanding at 2 cm/s. How fast is the volume changing when the edge is 5 cm?
A balloon is inflated so its radius increases at 1 cm/s. How fast is the volume increasing when r = 7 cm?
The radius of a circle increases at 0.7 cm/s. How fast is the circumference increasing?
questions.explanation: C = 2πr, so dC/dt = 2π(dr/dt) = 2π(0.7) = 1.4π cm/s. Notice this does not depend on r.

questions.q: A stone dropped in a pond makes circular ripples whose radius grows at 5 cm/s. How fast is the enclosed area growing when r = 8 cm?
If y = 7x³ and x increases at 2 units/s, at what rate is y changing when x = 1?
The length x of a rectangle decreases at 3 cm/min while the width y increases at 1 cm/min. When x = 10 and y = 6, how is the area changing?
questions.explanation: A = xy, so dA/dt = y(dx/dt) + x(dy/dt) = 6(−3) + 10(1) = −18 + 10 = −8, so the area is decreasing at 8 cm²/min.

faq.q: What does Exercise 6.1 of Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It covers the rate of change of quantities: using the derivative dy/dx (and the chain rule dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt)) to find how areas, volumes, perimeters and other quantities change with respect to time or another variable.

faq.q: What is the chain rule trick for related-rate problems?
faq.a: Write the quantity you want as a formula, differentiate both sides with respect to time t, and substitute the known rate. For a circle, A = πr² gives dA/dt = 2πr (dr/dt), so if you know dr/dt you can find dA/dt.

faq.q: Why does the perimeter of a square grow at a constant rate but the area does not?
faq.a: Perimeter P = 4x is linear, so dP/dt = 4(dx/dt) has no x in it. Area A = x² is quadratic, so dA/dt = 2x(dx/dt) still depends on the current side length x.

faq.q: What units should the answer carry in rate-of-change questions?
faq.a: The unit is the quantity's unit divided by the driving variable's unit. Area rate is cm²/s, volume rate is cm³/s, and a length rate is cm/s. Always write the unit in the final line to avoid losing marks.
